searchText: the eth chain being intergraded into ethereum is beacon. the eth1 miners are already mining blocks for beacon...........................its the continuation of blockchain. We are soft-launching a new ethereum consensus client https://github.com/sifraitech/grandine . Feedback is highly appreaciated ! Hard to give much feedback when it is closed source. Also, do you have any details of the vulnerabilities you have found in "all other implementations", or at least fed them back to the relevant teams? Thanks, we are working on open-sourcing it, but for now only binaries, so feel free to test it on isolated VM with some testnet. We started to report via Bounty Program, fork choice vulnerability was patched on other clients, but seems our bounty got stuck somewhere, good moment to ping <@!291925846556540928> 🙂 So this was a spec vulnerability, not an implementation vulnerability? That was a fork choice vulnerability introduced in the reference implementation. Other teams follow reference implemenations for complex parts such as fork choice. That's how it got into all other implementations. The spec didn't have this vulnerability. ``` tbehrens@WSL-INSIDERTEST:~$ ./grandine-linux-0.1.0 --network prater [2021-06-30T11:50:20.611-04:00] [INFO] [grandine] starting beacon node [2021-06-30T11:50:20.611-04:00] [INFO] [grandine] chain: prater [2021-06-30T11:50:20.611-04:00] [INFO] [grandine] data directory: "/home/tbehrens/.grandine/prater" [2021-06-30T11:50:20.612-04:00] [INFO] [grandine] Eth1 RPC URL: None [2021-06-30T11:50:20.612-04:00] [INFO] [grandine] graffiti: [] [2021-06-30T11:50:20.612-04:00] [INFO] [grandine] HTTP API address: 127.0.0.1:9001 [2021-06-30T11:50:20.612-04:00] [INFO] [grandine] archival epoch interval: 32 [2021-06-30T11:50:20.612-04:00] [INFO] [grandine] slasher enabled: false [2021-06-30T11:50:20.612-04:00] [INFO] [grandine::schema] initialized data directory with schema version 0.1.0 [2021-06-30T11:50:21.676-04:00] [WARN] [beacon_fork_choice_sifrai_array::storage] Latest state checkpoint was not found. Attempting to find stored state by iteration [2021-06-30T11:50:21.685-04:00] [WARN] [beacon_fork_choice_sifrai_array::storage] Latest state checkpoint was not found. Processing passed blocks: 0 [2021-06-30T11:50:21.691-04:00] [INFO] [http_api::warp] HTTP server listening on 127.0.0.1:9001 Illegal instruction ``` I am being obstinate though, this is my personal PC which is a 3rd-gen Intel Core, Ivy Bridge. I don't know of any cloud providers that have something that old heh, I thought no one is using that old CPUs 🙂 This might matter more. This is a VPS on AMD Epyc. ``` yorick@vmi460543:~$ ./grandine-linux-0.1.0 --network prater [2021-06-30T17:52:21.613+02:00] [INFO] [grandine] starting beacon node [2021-06-30T17:52:21.613+02:00] [INFO] [grandine] chain: prater [2021-06-30T17:52:21.613+02:00] [INFO] [grandine] data directory: "/home/yorick/.grandine/prater" [2021-06-30T17:52:21.613+02:00] [INFO] [grandine] Eth1 RPC URL: None [2021-06-30T17:52:21.613+02:00] [INFO] [grandine] graffiti: [] [2021-06-30T17:52:21.613+02:00] [INFO] [grandine] HTTP API address: 127.0.0.1:9001 [2021-06-30T17:52:21.613+02:00] [INFO] [grandine] archival epoch interval: 32 [2021-06-30T17:52:21.613+02:00] [INFO] [grandine] slasher enabled: false [2021-06-30T17:52:21.614+02:00] [INFO] [grandine::schema] initialized data directory with schema version 0.1.0 [2021-06-30T17:52:22.218+02:00] [WARN] [beacon_fork_choice_sifrai_array::storage] Latest state checkpoint was not found. Attempting to find stored state by iteration [2021-06-30T17:52:22.232+02:00] [WARN] [beacon_fork_choice_sifrai_array::storage] Latest state checkpoint was not found. Processing passed blocks: 0 [2021-06-30T17:52:22.238+02:00] [INFO] [beacon_fork_choice_sifrai_array::storage] saving store head_slot: 0 [2021-06-30T17:52:22.238+02:00] [INFO] [beacon_fork_choice_sifrai_array::storage] saving state on slot 0 [2021-06-30T17:52:22.382+02:00] [INFO] [beacon_fork_choice_sifrai_array::mutator] chain saved (finalized blocks: 1, unfinalized blocks: 0) [2021-06-30T17:52:22.439+02:00] [ERROR] [grandine] Io(Os { code: 98, kind: AddrInUse, message: "Address already in use" }) ``` `AMD EPYC 7282 16-Core Processor` are you already running some other client? Seems we need more informative message on which exactly port is taken I am stubborn old goat. Greta convinced me that I need to do my part, so I'm looking to replace my PC when it is 10 years old, not before. Ah yes that'd be it. I am. Be great if you could output the port. Is this using 9000 by default? I'm still not doing this quite right. if your run "grandine --help" you will see keys for ports Never mind you use 9001 for http Try again There we go. Like that. `./grandine-linux-0.1.0 --network prater --discovery-port 9010 --enr-udp-port 9010 --libp2p-port 9010` Shutdown could be a bit more graceful, ^C spits out a whole raft of WARN messages. ``` ^C[2021-06-30T17:57:18.935+02:00] [INFO] [grandine] Saving current chain before exit. Please wait... [2021-06-30T17:57:18.964+02:00] [WARN] [beacon_fork_choice_sifrai_array::messages] send to p2p failed because the receiver was dropped [2021-06-30T17:57:18.993+02:00] [WARN] [beacon_fork_choice_sifrai_array::messages] send to p2p failed because the receiver was dropped [2021-06-30T17:57:18.993+02:00] [WARN] [beacon_fork_choice_sifrai_array::messages] send to validator failed because the receiver was dropped [2021-06-30T17:57:18.998+02:00] [WARN] [beacon_fork_choice_sifrai_array::messages] send to p2p failed because the receiver was dropped [2021-06-30T17:57:18.998+02:00] [WARN] [beacon_fork_choice_sifrai_array::messages] send to validator failed because the receiver was dropped [2021-06-30T17:57:19.004+02:00] [WARN] [beacon_fork_choice_sifrai_array::messages] send to p2p failed because the receiver was dropped ``` Great to see a sixth client! yea, we are not happy with shutdown too, but it's just an internal message, not a real problem if you could try full sync and maybe even some validators - feedback would be very helpful! On your machine Prater full sync make take ~2 hours only, so Greta hopefully won't be very upset about that 🙂 <@!777935002263617576> Which language is this client implemented in? Just curious. Rust. I must say this decision extremely contributed to the performance, stability and memory consumption.
